analysis.title: The Volatility Paradox: Cheap Mag 7, Expensive Tech, And A Market On Edge
key_insights: Mag 7 implied volatility trades at a discount to the broader tech complex. The relative vol ratio sits at the 15th percentile over the past four years.
Nomura's McElligott flags aggressive upside call buying across Mag 7 ahead of earnings: AAPL 70k January $380 calls ($570mn delta), GOOGL $430mn delta, MSFT $630mn delta, about $1.6bn combined.
Positioning in Mag 7 is split. Long/short hedge fund rolling Mag 7 beta is near the 97th percentile, while mutual fund beta is near the 11th percentile.
The NDX/SPX implied vol spread compressed sharply after last week's blowout. The three-day compression was the largest in four years, but the 1-month ATM spread is still at the 94th percentile.
AMZN has pulled back from all-time highs but the longer-term uptrend is intact. The 200-day moving average sits slightly below current levels and there is no clear medium-term trend.
Goldman favors AMZN Dec 280/310 call spreads at $4.50 (19 delta, stock ref. $253.60) ahead of this week's earnings. The stock is about 10% below YTD highs and holding key support.
Goldman favors SPY November 6 $780 calls, positioning for clearing events that could push equities to new highs, with volatility expected to stay supported on a breakout.

Goldman favors EWY December 18 $180/$210 call spreads, arguing renewed AI momentum could trigger a positioning squeeze after heavy hedge fund selling. EWY has reclaimed its 200-day moving average for the first time since the breakdown.
Vol of vol has been extreme since mid-October. Skew remains well bid and downside protection is still in demand while price action is erratic.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman likes adding upside exposure ahead of earnings via Dec 280/310 call spreads. The recent tech deleveraging resembles July's setup, when AMZN rose 15% after earnings.

earnings_insights: AMZN earnings due this week. Goldman notes AMZN surged 15% after earnings in July following a similar deleveraging setup.
